recs.title: Do NLP Models Know Numbers? Probing Numeracy in Embeddings
recs.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
recs.summary: This work investigates the numerical reasoning capabilities of a state-of-the-art question answering model on the DROP dataset and finds this model excels on questions that require numerical reasoning, i.e., it already captures numeracy.

recs.title: Investigating the Limitations of Transformers with Simple Arithmetic Tasks
recs.summary: It is found that how a number is represented in its surface form has a strong influence on the model's accuracy, and this result bolsters evidence that subword tokenizers and positional encodings are components in current transformer designs that might need improvement.

recs.title: Exploring the Numerical Reasoning Capabilities of Language Models: A Comprehensive Analysis on Tabular Data
recs.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
recs.summary: A hierarchical taxonomy for numerical reasoning skills with more than ten reasoning types across four levels: representation, number sense, manipulation, and complex reasoning is proposed.

recs.title: Number Cookbook: Number Understanding of Language Models and How to Improve It
recs.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations
recs.summary: This work introduces a benchmark covering four common numerical representations and 17 distinct numerical tasks in four major categories, and finetune practical-scale LLMs on proposed NUPA tasks and finds that naive finetuning can improve NUPA a lot on many but not all tasks, and surprisingly, techniques designed to enhance NUPA prove ineffective for finetuning pretrained models.

recs.title: Do Language Models Understand Measurements?
recs.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
recs.summary: This study shows that PLMs lack the capability required for reasoning over measurements, and proposes a simple embedding strategy to better distinguish between numbers and units, which leads to a significant improvement in the probing tasks.

recs.title: Verb Physics: Relative Physical Knowledge of Actions and Objects
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: An approach to infer relative physical knowledge of actions and objects along five dimensions (e.g., size, weight, and strength) from unstructured natural language text is presented.

recs.title: Extracting Commonsense Properties from Embeddings with Limited Human Guidance
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: This work proposes and assess methods for extracting one type of commonsense knowledge, object-property comparisons, from pre-trained embeddings and shows that an active learning approach that synthesizes common-sense queries can boost accuracy.

recs.title: Diversify Your Datasets: Analyzing Generalization via Controlled Variance in Adversarial Datasets
recs.venue: Conference on Computational Natural Language Learning
recs.summary: This work extends the method to drive conclusions about a model’s ability to learn and generalize a target phenomenon rather than to “learn” a dataset, by controlling additional aspects in the adversarial datasets.

recs.title: Dissociating language and thought in large language models
recs.venue: Trends in Cognitive Sciences

recs.title: A Survey of Deep Learning for Mathematical Reasoning
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: This survey paper reviews the key tasks, datasets, and methods at the intersection of mathematical reasoning and deep learning over the past decade, and evaluates existing benchmarks and methods and discusses future research directions in this domain.

recs.title: Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision
recs.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: This work synthesizes best practices for representing numbers in text and articulate a vision for holistic numeracy in NLP, comprised of design trade-offs and a unified evaluation.

recs.title: TIMEDIAL: Temporal Commonsense Reasoning in Dialog
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: This paper presents the first study to investigate pre-trained LMs for their temporal reasoning capabilities in dialogs by introducing a new task and a crowd-sourced English challenge set, TimeDial, and reveals that the models fail to reason about dialog context correctly; instead, they rely on shallow cues based on existing temporal patterns in context.

recs.title: Commonsense Knowledge Reasoning and Generation with Pre-trained Language Models: A Survey
recs.venue: AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
recs.summary: A survey of commonsense knowledge acquisition and reasoning tasks, the strengths and weaknesses of state-of-the-art pre-trained models for commonsense reasoning and generation as revealed by these tasks, and reflects on future research directions are presented.

recs.title: Investigating Numeracy Learning Ability of a Text-to-Text Transfer Model
recs.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
recs.summary: This work investigates the ability of text-to-text transfer learning model (T5), which has outperformed its predecessors in the conventional NLP tasks, to learn numeracy, to struggle considerably in the extrapolation setting across all four tasks.

recs.title: Identify, Align, and Integrate: Matching Knowledge Graphs to Commonsense Reasoning Tasks
recs.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: This work presents an approach to assess how well a candidate KG can correctly identify and accurately fill in gaps of reasoning for a task, which is called KG-to-task match and demonstrates that ATOMIC, an event-inference focused KG, is the best match for SIQA and MCScript2.0, and that the taxonomic ConceptNet and WikiHow-based KGs are the bestmatch for PIQA across all 3 analysis phases.

recs.title: Beyond Output Matching: Bidirectional Alignment for Enhanced In-Context Learning
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: Bidirectional Alignment is proposed to fully leverage the models' preferences for ICL examples to improve the ICL abilities of student models and can consistently outperform existing baselines on a variety of tasks involving language understanding, reasoning, and coding.

recs.title: Injecting the score of the first-stage retriever as text improves BERT-based re-rankers
recs.venue: Discover Computing
recs.summary: A novel approach for combining first-stage lexical retrieval models and Transformer-based re-rankers is proposed, which injects the relevance score of the lexical model as a token into the input of the cross-encoder re-ranker.

recs.title: On the data requirements of probing
recs.venue: Findings
recs.summary: A novel method to estimate the required number of data samples in such experiments is presented and, across several case studies, it is verified that the estimations have sufficient statistical power.

recs.title: Predicting Numerals in Natural Language Text Using a Language Model Considering the Quantitative Aspects of Numerals
recs.venue: Workshop on Knowledge Extraction and Integration for Deep Learning Architectures; Deep Learning Inside Out
recs.summary: This paper measures the NCS acquired by existing neural language models using a masked numeral prediction task as an evaluation task and proposes methods to reflect not only the symbolic aspect but also the quantitative aspect of numerals in the training of language models, using a loss function that depends on the magnitudes of the numerals and a regression model for the masked numal prediction task.

recs.title: A survey on mathematical reasoning and optimization with large language models
recs.venue: Intelligent Systems with Applications

recs.title: How Large Are Lions? Inducing Distributions over Quantitative Attributes
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: This work proposes an unsupervised method for collecting quantitative information from large amounts of web data, and uses it to create a new, very large resource consisting of distributions over physical quantities associated with objects, adjectives, and verbs which it calls Distributions over Quantitative (DoQ).

recs.title: Deep Learning for Symbolic Mathematics
recs.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations
recs.summary: It is shown that neural networks can be surprisingly good at more elaborated tasks in mathematics, such as symbolic integration and solving differential equations, and a syntax for representing these mathematical problems, and methods for generating large datasets that can be used to train sequence-to-sequence models.

recs.title: Analysing Mathematical Reasoning Abilities of Neural Models
recs.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations
recs.summary: This paper conducts a comprehensive analysis of models from two broad classes of the most powerful sequence-to-sequence architectures and finds notable differences in their ability to resolve mathematical problems and generalize their knowledge.

recs.title: MAWPS: A Math Word Problem Repository
recs.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: MAWPS allows for the automatic construction of datasets with particular characteristics, providing tools for tuning the lexical and template overlap of a dataset as well as for filtering ungrammatical problems from web-sourced corpora.

recs.title: Analysis Methods in Neural Language Processing: A Survey
recs.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: Analysis methods in neural language processing are reviewed, categorize them according to prominent research trends, highlight existing limitations, and point to potential directions for future work.
